sanskrit: kathā dive asurāya bravāma kathā pitre haraye tveṣanṛmṇaḥ | pṛśniṃ varuṇa dakṣiṇāṃ dadāvān punarmagha tvaṃ manasācikitsīḥ ||
english: How shall we speak to the Asura of heaven, how to the tawny Father of fierce might? O Varuṇa, having given the dappled cow as the southern fee, O Punarmagha, thou hast deemed it good in thy mind.

sanskrit: na kāmena punarmagho bhavāmi saṃpṛcya kaṃ pṛśnim etām upāje | kena mat tvam atharvan kāvyena kena jātenāsi jātavedāḥ ||
english: Not by desire alone do I become Punarmagha, having consulted whom I brought near this dappled cow. By what wisdom art thou greater than I, O Atharvan? By what birth art thou Jātavedas?

sanskrit: satyam ahaṃ gabhīraḥ kāvyena satyaṃ jātenāsmi jātavedāḥ | na me dāso nāryo mahitvaṃ vrataṃ mīmāya yad ahaṃ dhariṣye ||
english: Truly I am profound in poetic wisdom; truly by my birth I am Jātavedas. Neither serf nor noble has measured the greatness of my vow which I shall uphold.

sanskrit: na tvad anyaḥ kavitaro na vedhā na dhīrataro varuṇa svadhāvaḥ | tvam aṅga viśvā janimāni vettha sa cin nu tvaj jano māyī bibhāya ||
english: No other is more skilled in vision, no fashioner, no one more steadfast than thou, O Varuṇa, possessor of thine own power. For thou, indeed, knowest all births; even the crafty man fears thee.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hy aṅga varuṇa svadhāvo viśvāni vettha janimā śardhanīte | kim enā rajasaḥ paro 'sti kim avareṇāvaram amura ||
english: For thou, O Varuṇa, possessor of thine own power, knowest all births, O thou before whom troops tremble. What is beyond yonder firmament? What is the lower beyond the lower, O unwearied one?

sanskrit: ekam enā rajasaḥ paro 'sti para ekena durdāśaṃ cid anyat | tat te vidvān varuṇa pra bravīmy adhovacasaḥ paṇayo bhavantu nīcair dāsā upa sarpantu riprāḥ ||
english: One thing is beyond yonder firmament; beyond the other lies yet another that is hard to see. This, knowing it, I declare to thee, O Varuṇa: let the Paṇis become speakers of what is beneath; let the defiled serfs creep low.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hy aṅga varuṇa pra bravīṣi punarmagheṣv avadyāni bhūri | mo ṣu paṇy abhy etāvatā bhūr mā tvā vocann arādhasaṃ janāsaḥ ||
english: For thou, O Varuṇa, dost proclaim many blameable deeds among the Punarmagh ones. Do not, then, fall upon the Paṇi by so much; let not people call thee ungracious.

sanskrit: mā mā vocann arādhasaṃ janāsaḥ punas te pṛśniṃ jaritar dadāmi | stotraṃ me viśvam ā yāhi janeṣv antar deveṣu mānuṣeṣu vipra ||
english: Let not people call me ungracious; again I give thee the dappled cow, O singer of praise. Come to me with all my hymn of praise among the folk, among the gods and among men, O sage.

sanskrit: ā te stotrāṇi vardhanāni yāmi dehi tan mahyaṃ yad adattam asti | yujyo naḥ saptapadaḥ sakhāsi samā nau bandhur varuṇaḥ samā jā ||
english: I come to thy praises that grant increase; give me that which is yet ungiven. Thou art our seven-paced companion in yoke, our equal kinsman is Varuṇa, equal in birth.

sanskrit: veda vai tad yan nau samā jā dadāmi tubhyaṃ yad adattam asti | devo devāya gṛṇate vayodhā vipro viprāya stuvate sumedhāḥ ||
english: I know indeed that which is our equal birth; I give thee what is yet ungiven. The god, life-sustaining, to the god who praises; the wise one of excellent insight to the wise one who lauds.

sanskrit: ajījano hi varuṇa svadhāvann atharvāṇaṃ pitaraṃ viśvadevam | tasmā urv āyuṣ kṛṇuhi praśastaṃ sakhā no 'si paramaś ca bandhuḥ ||
english: For thou, O Varuṇa, possessor of thine own power, didst beget Atharvan, the progenitor, the all-divine. Make for him a wide and laudable life span; thou art our friend and supreme kinsman.

sanskrit: vṛṣā me ravo nabhasā na tanyatur ugreṇa taṃ vacasā bādha id u te | ahaṃ tam asya grabhir agrabhaṃ rasaṃ jyotiṣeva tamasa ud eti sūryaḥ ||
english: My roar is like a bull, like thunder from the sky; with fierce speech I shall drive it away from thee. I have seized its essence with this my grip, as the sun rises from the darkness like a light.

sanskrit: yat te 'podakaṃ viṣaṃ tat ta āt tābhir agrabham | gṛhṇāmi madhyam uttamam utāvamaṃ bhiyasā neśad ād u te ||
english: Whatever waterless poison is thine, that of thine I have now seized with these means. I seize the middle, the highest, and also the lowest; by fear it shall not prevail, and now it is thine no more.

sanskrit: balena te balaṃ hanmi tanvā hanmi te tanum | viṣeṇa hanmi te viṣam ahe mṛṣīṣṭhā mā jīvīḥ pratyag abhy etu tvā viṣam ||
english: With strength I smite thy strength; with body I smite thy body. With poison I smite thy poison. O serpent, lie thou still; live not. Let the poison flow back and return upon thee.

sanskrit: asitasya taimātasya babhror apodakasya ca | sātrāsāhasya manyor jyām ugrasyeva dhanvano vi muñcāmi rathām̐ iva ||
english: Of the black serpent, of the Taimāta, of the brown one, of the waterless one, and of the wrath of the all-conquering — I loose the bowstring as of a fierce bow, as one unyokes chariots.

sanskrit: kailāta pṛśna upatṛṇya babhrav ā me śṛṇutāsitā alīkāḥ | mā naḥ sakhyuḥ kāmam api ṣṭhād āśrāvayāddho vīrṣe ramadhvam ||
english: O Kailāta, O dappled one, O Upatṛṇya, O brown one — listen to me, O black ones, O Alīkas. Do not stand in the way of our friend's desire. Make yourselves heard; indeed, be pleased, O serpents.

sanskrit: āliki ca vili pitā yas te mātā ca | vidma te viśvato bandhum arasa kiṃ kariṣyasi ||
english: Āliki and Vili are thy father and thy mother. We know thy kinsman on every side. Thou art made powerless — what wilt thou do?

sanskrit: urugūlāyā duhitā jātā dāsy asiknyāḥ | prataṅkaṃ dadruṣī nu sāhīn arasām̐ akaḥ ||
english: Daughter of Urugūlā, born of the slavegirl of the black one — she who was crawling about spreading her rash, has now rendered the powerful serpents powerless.

sanskrit: karṇā śvāvid abravīd girer avacarantikā | yāḥ kāś cemāḥ khanitrimās tāsām arasatamaṃ viṣam ||
english: The eared porcupine spoke, roaming at the foot of the mountain: 'Whatever burrowing creatures these are, their poison is the most powerless of all.'

sanskrit: tābuvaṃ na tābuvaṃ na ghed asi tvaṃ tābuvam | tābuvenārasaṃ viṣam ||
english: Not Tābuvam, not Tābuvam — thou art not really Tābuvam. By the Tābuvam the poison is made powerless.

sanskrit: tastuvaṃ na tastuvaṃ na ghed asi tvaṃ tastuvam | tastuvenārasaṃ viṣam ||
english: Not Tastuvam, not Tastuvam — thou art not really Tastuvam. By the Tastuvam the poison is made powerless.

sanskrit: arasaṃ te 'he viṣam iyaṃ kṛṇotv oṣadhiḥ | trāyamāṇā sahamānā sahasvatī sahātā id gor aśvāt puruṣād viṣam ||
english: May this herb render thy poison powerless, O serpent — the Trāyamāṇā, the overpowering one, the possessor of power, the prevailing one. It has surely expelled the poison from cow, from horse, from man.

sanskrit: yad āñjanaṃ traikakudaṃ jātaṃ himavatas pari | yātūṃś ca sarvān jambhayā sarvāś ca yātudhānyaḥ ||
english: O Āñjana with the three peaks, born from the Himavat — crush all the sorcerers and all the female demons of sorcery.

sanskrit: utevāsi paripāṇaṃ yātujambhanam āñjana | utāmṛtatvasyeśiṣa utāsi pitubhojanam ||
english: Thou art indeed a protector, a crusher of sorcerers, O Āñjana. Thou hast power over immortality, and thou art nourishment for the drink-offering.

sanskrit: paripāṇaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ paripāṇaṃ gavām asi | aśvānām arvatām it paripāṇāya tasthiṣe ||
english: Thou art the protection of men, the protection of cattle. For the protection of horses, of steeds, thou hast stood firm.

sanskrit: pari māṃ pari ṇaḥ priyaṃ pari ṇaḥ pāhi yad dhanam | arātir in no mā tārīn mā ca naḥ kiṃ canāmamat ||
english: Protect me, protect what is dear to us, protect our wealth. Let not enmity cross us; let nothing afflict us.

sanskrit: na taṃ prāpnoti śapatho na kṛtyā nābhiśocanam | nainaṃ viṣkandham aśnute yas tvā bibharty āñjana ||
english: No curse reaches him, no sorcery, no grief-causing spell. Viṣkandha does not afflict him who carries thee, O Āñjana.

sanskrit: āsan mantryād duṣvapnyāt kṣetriyāc chapathād uta | durhārdaś cakṣuṣo ghorāt tasmān naḥ pāhy āñjana ||
english: From the spell cast through the mouth, from evil dreaming, from hereditary disease, from the curse, and from the evil eye, from its terrible gaze — protect us from that, O Āñjana.

sanskrit: trayo dāsā āñjanasya takmā balāsa ād ahiḥ | varṣiṣṭhaḥ parvatānāṃ trikakun nāma te pitā ||
english: Three are the servants of Āñjana: fever, the consumptive disease Balāsa, and the serpent. Highest among mountains, Trikakud is the name of thy father.

sanskrit: vṛtrasyāsi kanīnikā parvatasyāsy akṣyau | devebhiḥ sarvaiḥ proktaṃ paridhir nāma vā asi ||
english: Thou art the pupil of Vṛtra's eye; thou art the two eyes of the mountain. Proclaimed by all the gods, thou art named Paridhi — the Encompasser.

sanskrit: vaido ha veda te nāma gandharvaḥ parivācanam | yata āñjana prajāyase tata ehy ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: The Gandharva Vaida knows thy name as a secret. From wherever thou art born, O Āñjana, come hither for the sake of our unharmed well-being.

sanskrit: yadi vāsi traikakudaṃ yadi yāmunam ucyase | ubhe te bhadre nāmnī tābhyāṃ naḥ pāhy āñjana ||
english: Whether thou art Traikakuda or art called Yamunā — both thy names are auspicious; by both of them protect us, O Āñjana.

sanskrit: yasyāñjana prasarpasy aṅgamaṅgaṃ paruṣparuḥ | tasmād yakṣmaṃ vi bādhasva- -ugro madhyamaśīr iva ||
english: Into whatever limb by limb, joint by joint thou dost creep, O Āñjana — drive out the disease Yakṣma from that place, like the fierce serpent that strikes at the middle.

sanskrit: nainaṃ ghnanti paryāyiṇo na sannām̐ ava gacchati | jane sa na pra mīyate yas tvā bibharty āñjana ||
english: The surrounding attackers do not slay him; he does not fall among the fallen. Among men he does not die who carries thee, O Āñjana.

sanskrit: idaṃ vidvān āñjana satyaṃ vakṣyāmi nānṛtam | saneyam aśvaṃ gāṃ vāsa ātmānaṃ tava pūruṣa ||
english: Knowing this, O Āñjana, I shall speak truly, not falsely. May I win the horse, the cow, the garment, and my own self, O thy man.
